## Profile

Marine climate-change ecologist and conservation scientist working on biodiversity redistribution, climate velocity, species distribution modelling, spatial ecology, and applied marine conservation.

My work connects global environmental datasets, ecological theory, reproducible workflows, and conservation decision-making, with a focus on how ocean warming reshapes biodiversity patterns and what that means for protected areas, climate adaptation, and ocean governance.

## Research Strengths

- Marine climate-change ecology and biodiversity redistribution.
- Climate velocity, climate exposure, marine climate refugia, and climate-smart conservation.
- Species distribution modelling, spatial ecology, oceanographic fronts, and marine megafauna.
- Conservation planning, marine protected areas, high-seas conservation, and policy-relevant science.
- Reproducible data science in R, spatial analysis, gridded climate products, Shiny, Git/GitHub, and Quarto.

## Teaching, Training, and Mentoring

Teaching and supervision interests include quantitative ecology, marine conservation, climate-change biology, R, spatial modelling, biodiversity data science, climate-model products, and reproducible research.

**Instructor, UCSB ESM240 Climate Change Biology**  
2023 and 2025. Designed and delivered graduate-level lectures, developed assignments, supervised projects, and evaluated coursework.

**Teaching Assistant, University of Queensland**  
2018 - 2020. Courses included Advanced Analysis of Scientific Data, Analysis of Scientific Data, Pharmacy Data Analysis and Professional Practice, Probability and Statistics in Engineering, Environmental Data Analysis, and Biostatistics and Experimental Design.

**Workshop organizer and contributor**  
Climate and Ocean Modeling Workshop at CERFACS, Climate Change and Marine Megafauna Workshop in Panama, Ocean Front Megafauna and Climate Change workshop at Acadia University, and Ocean Front and Climate Change workshop at Nelson Mandela University.

**Mentoring**  
Mentored graduate students and collaborators on Save the Blue Five climate-change assessment, megafauna-fisheries interactions, climate-smart closures for pelagic fisheries, high-seas conservation, and climate-proof marine protected areas.

Selected public teaching materials are available on the [Projects page](projects.qmd#workshops-and-teaching-materials), including climate-change biology practicals, ocean-front and marine-megafauna workshop material, climate-model tutorials in R, and Climate Data Operators training notes.

## Presentations and Service

Invited presentations include climate change in the ocean and conservation at Encuentro del Pacífico Sudeste in Panama, and climate velocity in the ocean and implications for conservation at ASLO. Conference contributions include IMPAC5, Species on the Move, Ocean Sciences Meeting, and the Sustainability, Research and Innovation Congress.

## Selected Outputs

- First-author publications in *Nature Climate Change* and *Trends in Ecology & Evolution* on climate velocity, deep-ocean biodiversity exposure, and climate-smart protected areas.
- Applied conservation-science contributions in *Nature*, *Nature Reviews Biodiversity*, *Ecological Applications*, and *Methods in Ecology and Evolution*.
- Interactive Shiny tools for ocean-climate downscaling products and marine megafauna occurrence data.
- Reproducible training and workshop material for students, collaborators, and conservation practitioners.

## Languages

Fluent Spanish and fluent English.
